title: Halftone Portrait
thesis: A human face rendered as a live halftone dot grid, drawn from video on a canvas one frame at a time. The component owns the render contract and the motion allocation; the consumer owns the media, the caption and the surrounding layout. The cutout is deliberately not a runtime concern: a matted source composited over a flat light plate reproduces the entire look for free, because a light plate maps to no dots, so the element carries no machine-learning runtime, no model weights and no network calls.
anatomy: Host box: square by default, radius panel 24, clipped. The only styled surface.
Source video: decode-only, muted, looped, inline, never displayed.
Sample canvas: offscreen, sized to the dot grid rather than the display.
Visible canvas: role=img with a consumer-supplied accessible label.
Dot grid: one dot per cell, radius driven by cell luminance.
Tone curve: auto-levels, then contrast, brightness and dot gamma.
Lattice: axis-aligned by default; rotated and staggered variants share one slower path.
Failure plate: the box keeps its size and states the reason.

renderContract.autoLevels: Per-frame 64-bin histogram, 2nd and 98th percentile stretched to the full range, eased 12 percent per frame so exposure changes do not pulse the grid.
renderContract.tone: darkness = (value - 0.5) * contrast + 0.5 + brightness, clamped, then raised to dotGamma.
renderContract.sampling: The offscreen canvas is sized to cols x rows, so the browser performs the downscale and getImageData reads one pixel per cell instead of the whole frame.
renderContract.devicePixelRatio: Clamped to 2. A 3x backing store triples fill cost with no visible gain at this dot size.
renderContract.path: All dots are added to a single path and filled once. A fill per dot is an order of magnitude slower at this density.

motion.default: Every instance mounts static. Under the default allocated policy the single most visible instance is handed the animation and yields it when another becomes more visible.
motion.repeated: Instances that are not animating hold a complete static halftone frame. They are not blank, dimmed or placeholder.
motion.reduced: prefers-reduced-motion paints one frame and never starts a render loop. The static frame carries the same meaning as the animation.
motion.failure: A missing source, a decode error or a tainted canvas releases motion, keeps the box and states the reason.
motion.autoplayRefused: Downgrades silently to the static frame already painted. No play control is fabricated.
motion.offscreen: An always-on instance idles the moment it leaves the viewport, so a long marquee never pays for portraits nobody can see.

mediaContract.preparation: The cutout is baked into the source before it reaches the browser. See pipeline provenance in fixtures/media/PROVENANCE.md.
mediaContract.rationale: Live segmentation costs an 11MB wasm runtime plus a per-frame neural network for a result that is fixed once a clip is approved.
mediaContract.expected: Square, muted, short loop, subject composited over a flat light plate.
componentNeverDoes: fetch media it was not given
run segmentation or any model at runtime

attributes.name: src
attributes.notes: Source video URL. Same-origin or CORS-enabled, otherwise the canvas taints and the element fails visibly.

attributes.name: label
attributes.notes: Accessible label for the rendered image.

attributes.name: grid-step
attributes.notes: Grid pitch in CSS pixels. Lower is finer and costs more.

attributes.name: max-radius
attributes.notes: Radius of a fully dark dot.

attributes.name: dot-gamma
attributes.notes: Radius response curve. Below 1 fattens midtones.

attributes.name: screen-angle
attributes.notes: Rotates the lattice, as a print screen angle does.

attributes.name: auto-levels
attributes.notes: Set to off to disable the per-frame histogram stretch.

attributes.name: dot-shape
attributes.notes: circle, square, diamond, cross or ring.

attributes.name: zoom
attributes.notes: Crop in. Never below 1: there is no source outside the frame.

attributes.name: motion-policy
attributes.notes: allocated or always. always opts out of the one-live allocation and is a bounded exception; see motionDecisionException.

lockedTreatment.note: The treatment approved on the originating surface. Carried here as evidence of intent, not as component authority: a consumer may set any supported attribute.

prohibited: more than one animated instance under the default allocated policy
running segmentation or any model at runtime
fetching a model, a runtime or media the consumer did not supply
a blank or placeholder box when motion is unavailable
hiding the subject under reduced motion
fabricating a play control when autoplay is refused
owning a quote, a name, an attribution or a consent state
owning card, marquee or section layout
outOfScope: the testimonial card, its quote typography and its attribution
the marquee or slider that may eventually carry several portraits
consent capture and evidence governance for a likeness
media preparation tooling, which lives with the pipeline that produces the clips

motionDecisionException.summary: Olli approved multiple simultaneously animated halftone portraits for the testimonial marquee on 2026-07-27. Website Motion 1.0.0 otherwise permits one expressive event in the viewport, and Global Navigation carries the equivalent bounded exception for five live cores. This exception is cheaper than that one: a halftone portrait costs a canvas fill, not a WebGL context or a neural network, and every instance still idles the moment it leaves the viewport. The exception applies only to instances that explicitly set the attribute. The default policy is unchanged, so a portrait dropped onto any other surface still allocates one live instance.
